title: Polestar has a new look with its Formula 2030 concept
gist: Geely-owned EV maker Polestar unveiled its Formula 2030 hatchback concept, a styling exercise previewing the next Polestar 2's nose and a new rear light signature, with physical controls and recyclable materials. Polestars can no longer be bought in the US because of bipartisan bans on Chinese-owned car brands.

insights.claim: Polestar cars can no longer be bought in the US because parent Geely is Chinese and banning Chinese-owned car brands has bipartisan support in Congress.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: US exclusion of Chinese-owned auto brands caps Polestar's addressable market and extends to Western-styled brands under Chinese ownership.
insights.quote: banning Chinese-owned car brands enjoys remarkable bipartisan support in Congress.
insights.locator: Perhaps only a small percentage of Ars readers

insights.claim: Polestar's Formula 2030 concept previews the next Polestar 2's nose and a Single Blade rear light signature for production cars, though Polestar has not committed to producing the hatchback itself.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Signals Polestar's next-gen Polestar 2 design direction; the concept itself is a styling exercise, not a product.
insights.locator: The nose is a good preview of the next Polestar 2

insights.claim: Polestar is adding physical rocker switches and rotary controllers for manual driving modes in the Formula 2030 interior, a first for the brand, even as it develops autonomous driving technology.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Reflects an industry pullback from all-touchscreen interiors toward physical controls.
insights.locator: Polestar says the four-seat interior pushes its usual minimalism

insights.claim: The Formula 2030 concept was designed for recyclability using monomaterials, fully recyclable door interiors, low-emission steel in the chassis and biocomposites like flax-based bComp in place of plastics and carbon fiber.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Circular-materials design is becoming a standard premium-EV differentiator, benefiting biocomposite and green-steel suppliers.
insights.locator: You can't really tell from the photos
